pr_body:
The original code did not account for the possibility of the date expression being prefixed with `-`.

Also add some tests to check the various scenarios where remote indexes and date expressions can be combined.

Note that the scenario where the index expression is: `-<date-exp-with-colons>` still may produce remote cluster error. This expression is not valid (since it starts with `-` without preceding wildcard) but the error message will be confusing. Fixing it to produce the correct message may be more complicated. 

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/112243

See also: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/100646
pr_title: Improve date expression/remote handling in index names
pr_comment: Hi @smalyshev, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

It looks like that index name cannot start with '-' character (and many others) see [Index names must meet the following criteria](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/indices-create-index.html#indices-create-api-path-params)

I think we need to validate index expression as a whole (after resolving datemath expression) and not subtracting starting characters beforehands.

@volodk85 not sure I understand what you're proposing. Do you mean `resolveDateMathExpression` should deal with `-`? I am a bit reluctant to mess with it since it's used in a lot of places and these places may have some assumptions already about how it works. Also, strictly speaking `-` is not part of date math expression, so should `resolveDateMathExpression` really deal with it? 
Or are you proposing some different approach? Please explain.

@volodk85 I thought about it a bit more and I think we shouldn't do any datemath resolving there at all. I mean, what is the question we're trying to answer there? It's whether we're dealing with a local index expression that looks like remote because datemath expression in it contains `:`. So that's what we should be checking for. If we check whether the string begins with `<` or `-<` we don't need to check anything else. If it does, it's not a remote because remotes can't have `<` in it. So that's the only check we need to do.

review_comment:
This seems to change semantics slightly so that we no longer assume a remote cluster definition if the expression says: `<abc:def`, where in the past, it would have to also have the closing `>`. This seems inadvertent?

I wonder if it was better to check for `-` as the first character and then probe the rest, just like the original code? It seems `-` is handled in this method (further down) already so seems appropriate.
`<abc:def` can not be a valid remote expression since remote name can not include `<`. So I think not handling it as a remote should be correct?

perhaps add a comment around `<` not being support as part of a remote cluster alias or index? I guess your point is that date math expressions are really the only scenario where this notation can be used?
Right, and the remote name, unlike index name, can't contain date math expressions. So if we see `<` we know there's no way it's a remote name.

I did a quick test of trying to create a remote that starts with "<" and it failed both in the elasticsearch.yml file and via the `PUT _cluster/settings` API call, so it seems correct to say that remote cluster aliases cannot start with that character.

I am not entirely sure I follow why this is a remote cluster test? IIUC, the original issue will happen in a single cluster setup too? I also think the search only addresses a single cluster. Should we move this to a different IT to make this clear?

I need to test that both remote & local scenarios work fine - i.e. that scenarios that include valid remotes with date expressions work, and scenarios that include date expressions that look like remote but aren't work. If I only test it on single cluster, I may have broken the valid remote case but I wouldn't know that, as AFAIK we presently don't have any tests that verify this scenario.
Maybe we need tests in two places then? Regular tests to verify the local only scenario, and this one to verify the cross-cluster scenario?
Nice! I need to add similar tests to CrossClustersQueryIT for ESQL.

nit: can you clarify in the comment what the `-` means? I think it means to exclude it from the search, right?
Also: nit: the code comment ends with a comma, which could be removed
